name: KeyOrder Settle Fast Path

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

primaryTarget: native release build, criterion benches (macOS arm64)
hypothesisMarkdown:
## KeyOrder Settle Fast Path Hypothesis

### Hypothesis

`KeyOrder::settle` runs before every insertion and move. It always calls `reclaim`, which drains `..head` from the key and ticket vectors even when `head == 0`, and the post-hasher profile of a 10k-row cache pipeline load attributes ~10% of samples to `settle`. Returning early when there are no removed head slots and no pending removals makes the common append path skip that work.

### Scope Lock

**Tested mechanism:** early return in `settle`/`reclaim` when nothing is pending.
**Allowed changes:** `crates/src/collections/key_order.rs` (`settle`, `reclaim`).
**Forbidden in this experiment:** insert lookup changes, reindex changes, callers.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
### Measurement Plan

KeyOrder unit tests and full lib tests (KeyOrder is shared); clippy/fmt. Bench `hot_paths` cache-hot, `keyed_sort`, `sort_and_page`, `live_group` vs base. Pass: cache-hot/load >=5% faster.
